title: Qualify short-tail Uniform merging at 40 GiB
question: Does the 8 GiB opt-in retention decision transfer structurally and in complete-job time to a 40 GiB run with a 256 MiB engine setting?
summary: One matched 40 GiB pair reduced elapsed 5.83%, CPU 1.09%, and temporary reads/writes 16.84%. Cache refaults rose 38.94%. The original 8 GiB retention remains Linux raw opt-in.

workloads: 40 GiB fixed-width CSV, terminal Uniform and eight exact parts, 256 MiB engine, one worker, hard 1 GiB cgroup without swap.

validation.summary: Exact independent 40 GiB oracle and native manifest cleanup. Linux default, all-feature, and raw-feature full lint/tests pass, portable WASM and WASI compilation pass. Separate Windows ordinary storage/direct checks with Linux route inactive. Default native binaries restored.

limitations: Single full matched pair with control first and uncontrolled WSL2 backing cache.
Windows validates fallback compilation and ordinary behavior. The performance path is raw native Linux only.
Descriptor observation is a point, not a maximum.
exclusions: Large elapsed and CPU comparison excludes fixture identity and verification. Filesystem counters and file-cache refaults are distinct from managed logical traffic.
reopen_when: Require new platform, workload and resource eligibility evidence before considering automatic selection or default delivery.
